thread:
Samira Patel: Ran a quick perf sweep on fp8 vs int8 on A100s this morning. FP8 kernels are faster on long sequences but we see a 8-12% tail latency increase for short sequences when batching.
Alex R: Interesting — are you using per-channel calibration or per-tensor? small details can flip FP8 accuracy/perf.
Samira Patel: Per-channel for the main run. Used our usual calibration set (~5k samples). Also tried per-tensor for a spot check and FP8 latency improved for short seqs but perplexity regressed slightly.
Jia Chen: Did you warm up the KV cache before measuring tail latency? We saw the cache miss penalty skew short seq numbers.
Samira Patel: Good call. Warmup was 0. I re-ran with a 2-step warmup (prefill 1 token then real request) and tail improved ~4% for FP8.
Connor Lee: What's the batching heuristic? adaptive batching might aggregate short requests into longer effective sequences and change kernel selection.
Samira Patel: Using continuous batching with max_batch=32 and seq bucket 1/8/32. Kernel selector picks fp8-matmul for longer buckets, int8 for short ones currently.
Alex R: That's probably why. If per-tensor FP8 reduces quant noise, maybe we should prefer fp8 kernel for short buckets when calibration set shows low outlier rates.
Jia Chen: Question — how are we handling outliers in calibration? clipping vs rejection? That affects per-channel scales a lot.
Samira Patel: We clip at 0.999 quantile by default. Tried rejection of top 0.1% and saw more stable per-channel scales, fewer spikes, FP8 accuracy recovered.
Connor Lee: Rejection seems promising but can bias scale if calibration set isn't representative. What if we use a hybrid: clip per-tensor, reject per-channel outliers >3σ?
Alex R: Also consider stratified calibration: ensure calibration set contains short/long seqs and token diversity similar to real traffic. Otherwise kernel routing decisions will be misleading.
perf-bot: perf-bot: nightly-bench finished: fp8 w/ reject-top0.1% + KV-warmup reduced 95p latency by 7% vs baseline.
Jia Chen: Nice. Next steps: (1) run A/B where kernel selector prefers fp8 for short buckets if outlier_rate<0.5% (2) validate on parked-prod traces (3) run eval suite for generation quality.
Samira Patel: I'll set up the A/B and add a perf flag. Keeping calibration metadata (outlier_rate, method, sample_size) in metadata store would help reproduce.
Connor Lee: Agreed. Add a quick doc in eng-ml/bench that outlines the calibration policy and kernel routing heuristic. Short thread, actionable.
Alex R: I'll review the A/B config once it's up. :thumbsup:
